item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
STATUS OF EMRSs IN WEST BENGAL
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the  Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the scheme of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for providing quality education to tribal students in their own environment preserving local art and culture. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country. In West Bengal 9 EMRSs have been approved and all are functional. None of the blocks in Alipurduar districts fulfil the prescribed criteria for establishing EMRS.

National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, provides overall policy direction, academic support, monitoring, capacity building, recruitment, standardization of processes and implementation of the EMRS Scheme across the country. State EMRS Societies oversee the implementation, administration and day-to-day management of EMRSs within their jurisdictions. District Level EMRS Committees, under the Chairmanship of the District Collector/District Magistrates do local oversight and resolve local implementation issues.

The status of sanctioned, operational and under construction EMRSs in West Bengal, district wise is given at Annexure.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Vigyan TECH 2026 initiative
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi

‘विज्ञान Tech’, a first of its kind national initiative was organized by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), on National Technology Day, 11 May 2026 at BRIC-National Institute of Immunology (BRIC-NII), N. Delhi. The purpose was to promote a whole-of- Government approach for science, technology and innovation.

 

The exhibition brought together the technological strengths of 14 Ministries and Departments of the Government of India with strong R&D linkages through their autonomous institutes and laboratories and more than 100 in-house developed technologies were showcased. Based on a “Whole-of-Government” approach, technologies were showcased across key sectors such as Space and Geospatial Technologies; Climate and Agri-Food Technologies; Biopharma and Health Technologies; Bioindustrial and Green Chemicals; Deep-tech Materials and Advanced Engineering Technologies; Electronics, Semiconductors and Energy; and Deep-Sea and Atmospheric Technologies. The event also saw the release of ‘TECH-संग्रह’, a compendium featuring nearly 300 technologies developed by the participating institutions. Many of these technologies have already been commercialized or licensed, while others are progressing toward deployment to support national development goals.

 

The event witnessed several technology transfers/licensing of technologies to industry. The details are as follows:

 

DBT- Biotechnology Research & Innovation Council (DBT-BRIC)

 

  1. Accelerated Crop Innovation Technology platform
  2. Active dried yeast technology
  3. Enzyme for optimised lignocellulosic degradation technology
  4. CleverCUP
  5. NCE for Inflammatory Bowel Diseases

 

Indian Council For Medical Research (ICMR)

 

  1. Factor VIII Inhibitor Test for Haemophilia A Disorder
  2. PSP94 ELISA
  3. Multiplex Real-Time RT-PCR for Detection of Dengue Chikungunya and Zika Viruses

 

Council for Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR)

 

  1. CSIR PRIMA ET-11, 100% electric compact tractor

 

Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)

 

  1. Extruded Products technology
  2. Hybrid Green House Solar dryer
  3. Protein & Fiber rich Granola Bar

 

The following were also launched during the event:

 

Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

 

  1. Indigenous Glacier Lake Bathymetry Survey Solution developed by C-DAC, Thiruvananthapuram

 

Council for Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR)

 

  1. CSIR@100, a booklet outlining CSIR’s roadmap towards 2042 with a strong focus on deep-tech innovation, translational research, and technologies aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

 

The initiative served as a common strategic platform for knowledge exchange, technology showcasing and exploring opportunities to bridge the gap between laboratory research and industrial application. By bringing together various Ministries, policymakers, scientists, young researchers, industry leaders, and startup founders, the initiative strengthened connections across the innovation ecosystem and provided valuable insights into new opportunities for collaboration and innovation. This is a significant step towards breaking institutional silos as we embark on our journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

 

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Science and Technology & Ministry of Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

NKR/AK/MJ/NM

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Establishment of VDVKs in Tribal Areas of Rajasthan
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the population and percentage of Scheduled Tribes across Udaipur, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh, Banswara, Sirohi, Salumbar, Rajsamand and Chittorgarh districts of Rajasthan, block-wise is given at Annexure I.

Under Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) a total of 283 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) covering 85,349 beneficiaries have been sanctioned in Udaipur, Salumbar, Dungarpur and Pratapgarh districts of Rajasthan. The beneficiaries are engaged in the value addition, processing and marketing of locally available Minor Forest Produce (MFP) and agricultural produce such as graded wheat, wheat flour, daliya, maize, chana/chana dal, moong dal, urad dal, mango pickle (aam achar), turmeric powder, chilli powder, honey, soyabean products, herbal and amla-based products. item.title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental outcomes of BioE3 Policy
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental outcomes of BioE3 Policy Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:06PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Biotechnology under the Ministry of Science and Technology, under the aegis of BioE3 ( Bio technology for E conomy, E nvironment and E mployment) policy, has identified measurable targets in terms of scales, yield and Technology Readiness Level for technology development and scale up thereof for biomanufacturing of the bio-based alternatives to replace fossil-based inputs. Department of Biotechnology (DBT) also…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental outcomes of BioE3 Policy
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Biotechnology under the Ministry of Science and Technology, under the aegis of BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) policy, has identified measurable targets in terms of scales, yield and Technology Readiness Level for technology development and scale up thereof for biomanufacturing of the bio-based alternatives to replace fossil-based inputs. Department of Biotechnology (DBT) also supported the projects to develop the biomanufacturing solutions targeted to reduce the import dependency of fossil-based inputs. The digital portal ‘Sujivika’ launched by the DBT provides biotech import data. The portal facilitates identification of indigenous bio-based products based on import data for Atmanirbhar Bharat, targeting to promote domestic manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported chemicals and materials including the fossil-derived chemicals, materials and fuels.

 

Department has supported research, pilot-scale, and demonstration projects to convert agricultural residues, municipal organic waste, and industrial biogenic waste into advanced fuels, chemicals, and materials for industrial applications. The supported initiatives focus on the development of indigenous technologies for biomass pretreatment, biocatalysts, microbial bioprocesses, and integrated bio-refinery platforms to enable efficient utilization of diverse biomass feedstocks to bring in sustainability integrated with biomanufacturing value chain.  

 

The government through series of consultations with technical expert committees, thematic expert groups, and stakeholder consultations, has assessed potential biotech interventions and technologies that can contribute to India’s Carbon Emission Reduction and Net Zero Commitments.

 

The BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) policy is being implemented through inter-ministerial coordination involving relevant Ministries and Departments to promote convergence and joint efforts. Adapting to the converging and whole of the government approach, the department under the ambit of BioE3  (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) policy is working closely with line ministries and Departments for integration of the Bio-Enablers such as bio foundries and Bio AI Hubs to provide the scale, strengthening biomass supply chains, technology development, scale-up, mapping of high value chemicals, APIs, enzymes, Smart Proteins etc for further commercialization and regulatory aspects for biomanufacturing.

 

Following the accepted principles of circular economy and net zero emission, the BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) policy provides the platform to develop and demonstrate the pilot and pre-commercial scale bio manufacturing solutions for replacing the fossil-based inputs, and to promote the low carbon economy. Key performance indicators for environmental outcomes and progress towards circular bioeconomy include, but, not limited to providing technological solutions to reduce land use, inculcate renewability, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, waste-to-value solutions, and indigenized clean tech solutions through bio manufacturing. Aligning to the indicators for environment outcomes and circular economy, the Department supported major interventions such as biorestoration of degraded ecosystems like Sunderbans, Molecular tools for protected area conservation, Alternatives to single-use-plastics and polymers, converting lignocellulosic, industrial, and organic waste to sustainable aviation fuels, specialty chemicals and biomaterials, engineered enzymes for waste valorization and Carbon Capture Utilization Integrated Bimanufacturing.

 

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Science and Technology & Ministry of Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

*****

NKR/AK/MJ/NM

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Tribal Affairs DISPLACEMENT OF STs IN TIGER RESERVE AREAS Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:06PM by PIB Delhi The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) is mandated to inquire into complaints regarding the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Tribes which include issues related to alienation, development, atrocities, forest right claims, etc. including displacement of Scheduled Tribes from Tiger Reserve areas on a case-to-case basis and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
DISPLACEMENT OF STs IN TIGER RESERVE AREAS
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) is mandated to inquire into complaints regarding the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Tribes which include issues related to alienation, development, atrocities, forest right claims, etc. including displacement of Scheduled Tribes from Tiger Reserve areas on a case-to-case basis and makes appropriate recommendations to the concerned authorities, wherever warranted.

A few representations regarding voluntary village relocation from Tiger Reserves have been forwarded to the NTCA by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST). It has been clarified that the process of relocation of villages from Core/Critical Tiger Habitats is voluntary as per the provisions of Section 38 V (5) of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 2006, and Section 4(2) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006. The National Tiger Conservation Authority (Normative Standards for Tourism activities and Project Tiger) Guidelines, 2012, issued under section 38 O (1) (c) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, are also available in the public domain which clearly outline the principle of voluntary relocation which has been reiterated to all State Governments in different forms, from time to time.

The implementation of village relocation is undertaken by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations in accordance with the prescribed guidelines, and District Level Committees are constituted by the concerned States and Union Territories to facilitate effective implementation. The Guidelines issued by this authority provide for a rehabilitation package for voluntary village relocation, including settlement of rights, agricultural land and house construction etc. The framework also provides for provision of basic amenities and convergence with other Government schemes to ensure that relocated families are able to access welfare and development benefits. The financial assistance for voluntary relocation has been enhanced from ₹10 lakh to ₹15 lakh per family in 2021. Insofar as the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is concerned, the State Governments and UT Administrations have been exhorted to ensure that no rightful beneficiary is deprived of their forest rights, including compliance with Section 4(5) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006, which stipulates that the claimants cannot be evicted or removed from forest land under their occupation till the recognition and verification procedure is complete.

The National Tiger Conservation Authority has reiterated to all Tiger Range States that village rehabilitation shall be completely voluntary and that informed consent of the Gram Sabha and the concerned people shall be obtained before undertaking rehabilitation. The States have been advised to undertake voluntary village relocation in accordance with the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and the guidelines issued by this authority. The National Tiger Conservation Authority (Normative Standards for Tourism activities and Project Tiger) Guidelines, 2012, issued under section 38 O (1) (c) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, are also available in the public domain which clearly outline the principle of voluntary relocation which has been reiterated to all State Governments in different forms, from time to time. Consultations with the Gram Sabha are conducted by the respective State Governments which carry out thorough due diligence which incorporate prior informed consent and voluntariness as enshrined in the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006.

In order to ensure transparency of process, the said guidelines recommend that the relocation process could be monitored and implemented by the two committees namely, State Level Monitoring Committee & District Level Implementing Committee which consists of representatives from tribal welfare department too. Accordingly, an institutional mechanism for monitoring voluntary village relocation is already provided under the existing framework, and the concerned State Governments undertake relocation in accordance with the prescribed statutory provisions and guidelines. It is to be informed that there are no reports of involuntary or coerced relocation reported to this authority by the State-level Monitoring Committees and District-level Implementing Committees, which are mandated to oversee the process.

RN/

*****

(Release ID: 2298801)

The annual family income limits prescribed under the guidelines of these schemes are as under: S. No. Name of Scheme Annual Family Income Limit 1 Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST students…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
“EDUCATION AND HOUSING SCHEMES FOR STS IN KERALA”
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the following five ongoing scholarship schemes for Scheduled Tribe (ST) students across the country, including the State of Kerala. The annual family income limits prescribed under the guidelines of these schemes are as under:

S. No.

Name of Scheme

Annual Family Income Limit

1

Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class IX and X)

Rs. 2.50 lakhs

2

Post Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class XI and above)

Rs. 2.50 lakhs

3

National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students (Top Class)

Rs. 6.00 lakhs

4

National Fellowship for Higher Education for ST students (NFST)

No Income Limit

5

National Overseas Scholarship for ST students (NOS)

Rs. 6.00 lakhs

 

Apart from this, 'National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes, extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe persons for undertaking any income generation activities/ self-employment including education loan through its implementing agencies across the country including the state of Kerala. In case of individuals, having annual family income not exceeding ₹ 3 lakh p.a. both for rural and urban areas are eligible for availing concessional loans under the NSTFDC schemes.

In addition to above education support provided by the Central Government, as informed by the State Govt. of Kerala, it is also running its own Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme under which benefit is provided to all eligible ST students without any prescribed criteria of annual family income.

The intervention of housing under PM JANMAN scheme of this Ministry is being implemented by Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) through PMAY-G scheme. As per the approved norms, there is no prescribed annual income limit for sanctioning of awas to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) beneficiaries. However, there are only two (02) exclusion criteria in respect of PVTG households – (i) household with pucca houses and (ii) Household with any member as a government employee.

Further, housing assistance is also provided by the State Govt. of Kerala through their LIFE Mission. As per the guidelines of the LIFE Mission Scheme, the annual family income ceiling prescribed for availing housing benefits is ₹3.00 lakh.

As per the information received from State Govt. of Kerala, the majority of the Scheduled Tribe population in Kerala belongs to the economically weaker sections. It has not come to the notice of the State Government that a large number of Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries are being excluded from housing schemes on account of the prescribed income limit. In cases where Scheduled Tribe families are not eligible for housing assistance under the LIFE Mission due to prescribed income ceiling, they may be considered for housing assistance under the housing schemes implemented by the Scheduled Tribes Development Department, Govt. of Kerala. With regard to educational assistance, the question does not arise since there is no prescribed annual family income in the State Govt. of Kerala.

The appraisal and approval of the Expenditure Finance Commission (EFC) for their continuation of schemes implemented by M/o Tribal Affairs during F.Y. 2026-27 to 2030-31 is currently ongoing wherein, inter-alia, the proposal to revise the annual family income ceiling is included for seeking the approval of the Dept. of Expenditure on the draft EFC. The decision regarding enhancing the annual income limit under the said schemes in the EFC is subject to the approval of the Competent Authority.

RN/

  17. Space Kidz India,
  18. TakeMe2Space Technologies Pvt. Ltd,

 

The applications for usage and access to ISRO infrastructure (including the launch pads at ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota) are processed as per the standard SOP based on the application received by IN-SPACe on its Digital Platform and the readiness aspects are reviewed by an Expert Committee of IN-SPACe.

 

The total number of commercial rockets are proposed to be launched by Indian private companies over the next two years are as under:

 

FY 26-27: 02 nos.

FY 27-28: The Launch manifest is yet to be approved by IN-SPACe. It is expected that more than 06 nos. of launches may be undertaken by Indian Private Companies.

 

This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and

Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today

Aditya-L1 , launched on 2nd September 2023, is India’s first space-based solar observatory, placed in Halo orbit around Sun-Earth…
item.content:encoded:
Department of Space
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATIONS OF SPACE TECHNOLOGY
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:03PM by PIB Delhi

The major satellite missions launched during the last three years are given below:

  • Chandrayaan-3, launched on 14th July 2023, achieved the first-ever soft landing near the Moon’s south polar region on 23rd August 2023, and demonstrated safe landing, rover navigation, Sulphur detection and lunar soil temperature measurements.
  • Aditya-L1, launched on 2nd September 2023, is India’s first space-based solar observatory, placed in Halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1 in January 2024 to study the solar corona, photosphere and chromosphere.
  • XPoSat, launched on 1st January 2024, is India’s first dedicated X-ray polarimetry mission to study bright astronomical X-ray sources, including pulsars and black holes, under extreme conditions.
  • SPADEX (Space Docking Experiment), launched on 30th December 2024, demonstrated autonomous docking/undocking, power transfer and circumnavigation, making India the 4th country to demonstrate space docking technology for future lunar and human space missions.
  • NISAR, launched on 30th July 2025, is the first dual-frequency (L & S Band) radar Earth observation satellite, jointly developed by NASA and ISRO for global microwave imaging using fully polarimetric and interferometric data.
  • GSAT-7R (CMS-03) is India’s most advanced indigenously developed military communications satellite, designed to enhance the strategic communication capabilities of the Indian Navy.

 

Major applications of space technology undertaken during last three years by ISRO/DoS are:

  • Agriculture: Satellite-based crop area/yield estimation, crop monitoring and soil-moisture products supported national programmes and PMFBY across major crops and States; GeoCREST, Potato Crop Monitoring System and VEDAS-based geospatial yield estimation were operationalised.
  • Disaster Management: Near-real-time satellite-based monitoring of floods, landslides, cyclones, forest fires, GLOFs and droughts supported disaster response; over 890 flood products and alerts for more than 11 major landslide events were disseminated through MHA, NDMA, States, BHUVAN and NDEM.

Landslide Atlas of India was developed and techniques for landslide alerts using susceptibility, InSAR-based slope movement and rainfall thresholds are being developed; flood early warning and forest-fire alert services are operational, including eight daily observations with <30 min turnaround time.

  • Governance:
  1. Geospatial technologies supported planning and monitoring of MGNREGA, WDC-PMKSY, Panchayat assets and disaster management through Yuktdhara, Bhuvan Panchayat and NDEM; about 6.93 crore MGNREGA and 6.89 lakh watershed activities have been geotagged.
  2. National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM 5.0), released in June 2024, provides sub-metre satellite data, multilingual data labels and near-real-time disaster alerts, forming a core geospatial solution for the Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response (ICR-ER).
  3. Space technology supported Urban Frame Survey, Green Cover Index for National Highways, UIDAI navigation, property-tax mapping, urban water management, AMRUT 2.0, disaster management, telecom services and Digital Postal Address (DIGIPIN) initiatives.
  • Satellite Communication: Space technology supports BharatNet and Digital India by extending connectivity to rural areas and enabling broadband, secure government and strategic communications, DTH, VSAT, in-flight/maritime connectivity, tele-education, tele-medicine and disaster management.

Further, IN-SPACe, through its various initiatives and schemes, is collaborating with Non-Government Entities (NGEs) to develop innovative applications of space technology across key sectors such as agriculture, disaster management, and governance. To promote the development of advanced, technology-driven solutions, the following high-impact use cases have been identified for implementation by NGEs:

    1. Pest and disease forecasting and early detection systems for major crops across India.
    2. AI/ML-based systems for crop acreage estimation, yield assessment, and production forecasting.
    3. Development of crop insurance support and weather advisory systems.
    4. SAR-based agricultural applications leveraging NISAR data for irrigation planning and management.
    5. Reservoir rim slope stability monitoring to mitigate dam failure risks and associated disasters.
    6. Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) monitoring and Early Warning Systems.
    7. Development of Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) solutions.
    8. Decision Support Systems (DSS) for power sector infrastructure monitoring and Right-of-Way (RoW) management.
    9. Urban infrastructure information systems and smart governance solutions.

 

ISRO's major upcoming missions include the Gaganyaan, Venus Orbiter Mission, Chandrayaan-4 mission and Lunar Polar Exploration Mission / Chandrayaan-5.

  • Gaganyaan: India’s first human spaceflight programme, aimed at demonstrating human spaceflight capability by carrying Indian astronauts to Low Earth Orbit and safely returning them to Earth.
  • Venus Orbiter Mission: India's first dedicated mission to study the atmosphere, surface, and geological environment of Venus.
  • Chandrayaan-4 Mission: A lunar lander and lunar sample return mission. The major objective of Chandrayaan-4 mission is to successfully land on lunar surface, extract lunar sample through robotic arm, ascent from lunar surface and bring back the collected lunar regolith to Earth.
  • Lunar Polar Exploration (LUPEX) / Chandrayaan-5 Mission: The Chandrayaan-5 is a joint collaborative mission between ISRO and JAXA.  The mission will deploy a lander and rover to conduct in-situ studies of lunar surface and subsurface resources, supporting future sustained lunar exploration.

 

This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

****

NKR/AK/NM

(Release ID: 2298798)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
STRENGTHENING PM-JANMAN for PVTGs
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed in Lok Sabha today that Hon'ble Prime Minister launched Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for socio-economic development of 75 PVTG communities residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide basic facilities to improve their socio-economic conditions such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities. These objectives are being met through 11 interventions implemented by 9-line Ministries. . The details of the benefits given under PM JANMAN, as on 30.06.2026, Ministry-wise & State-wise, are given at Annexure I.

The review has noted that Phase-I has established a nationwide community-based capacity-building framework for strengthening last-mile governance in tribal areas. The programme…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 2:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has reviewed the implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan on a continuous basis through periodic monitoring at the Ministry, State and district levels. The review has noted that Phase-I has established a nationwide community-based capacity-building framework for strengthening last-mile governance in tribal areas. The programme aims to create a cadre of trained government functionaries, community leaders, women’s collectives and tribal youth to facilitate responsive governance across approximately one lakh tribal villages in 30 States/UTs.

The programme has made significant progress towards developing transformative tribal leadership by creating a large cadre of trained grassroots leaders drawn from government institutions as well as tribal communities. The achievement made in developing transformative Tribal leadership through the abhiyan during phase 1 is as follow:

  1. Approx. 15 lakh Adi Karmayogis mobilised through a cascading training architecture.

  2. More than 210 State Master Trainers, 2,200+ District Master Trainers and 11,000+ Block Master Trainers developed.

  3. 6,79,309 Adi Saathis and 4,03,306 Adi Sahyogis mobilised.

  4. 62,187 Tribal Village Vision 2030 Plans approved through Gram Sabhas.

  5. 54,324 Village Workbooks and 56,422 Adi Sewa Kendras (ASKs) recorded under the programme.

The Ministry has established an institutional mechanism to ensure continuity of capacity building, mentoring and follow-up support through Adi Sewa Kendras (ASKs) and Adi Karmayogi Volunteers (AKVs).

The programme strengthens community leadership and participatory development by placing Gram Sabhas and tribal communities at the centre of local planning and implementation. During Phase-I, communities undertook household surveys, transect walks, focus group discussions and development-gap assessments, culminating in preparation of Tribal Village Vision 2030 documents and Village Action Plans covering health, education, livelihoods, housing, drinking water, connectivity, financial inclusion and social protection. Gram Sabhas formally approved these plans, thereby institutionalising participatory decision-making.

Under this mechanism, the following mechanism is contributing to strengthening community leadership and participatory development in tribal areas:

  1. Adi Sewa Kendras (ASK) function as village-level single-window facilitation centres for information dissemination, entitlement facilitation, grievance redressal support and convergence with line departments.

  2. Adi Karmayogi Volunteers (AKV), selected from local tribal youth, support day-to-day functioning of ASKs, assist citizens in accessing government schemes, documentation, grievance registration, Gram Sabha processes, awareness campaigns and periodic updating of village development priorities.

  3. Mapping of ASKs and registration of AKVs enables authenticated records, location-based monitoring and evidence-based strengthening of village institutions.

  4. Weekly monitoring by the Ministry, States and district administrations has been instituted to ensure effective implementation and sustainability of these village-level governance structures.

****

RN/  

(Release ID: 2298794)

The Government is committed to achieve saturation of telecom connectivity in underserved tribal areas. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
STATUS OF VAN DHAN VIKAS KENDRA CLUSTERS
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial support for establishment of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) through Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Limited (TRIFED) under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN). As on date 4,712 VDVKs, covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries, have been sanctioned in 28 States/UTs, with a total sanctioned amount of Rs. 642.19 crore under both the schemes out of which 3,406 VDVKs are operational. A maximum amount of Rs 15.00 lakhs is provided to State Governments to set up one VDVK for incurring the expenditure on raw material, training and capacity building, tool kits and machinery, mentoring charges, packaging and branding, transportation, storage etc. Revolving working capital is not provided to VDVKs under the schemes.

However, under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) component of the scheme, revolving fund is provided to State Implementing Agencies (SIAs) for undertaking Minor Forest Produce (MFP) procurement from tribal MFP gatherers at MSP, in case the market price falls below the MSP. During the Financial Year 2025–26, an amount of Rs. 2.50 crore has been released to the State Implementing Agency (SIA) of Meghalaya for the procurement of MFP.

 Fund release for establishment of VDVKs is undertaken through Treasury Single Account (TSA) system introduced by Ministry of Finance. TSA accounts have been opened by almost all State Implementing Agencies, and funds are being transferred to the TSA accounts of the SIAs. TSA system provides the treasury and central bank total oversight over liquidity, eliminates idle cash parked in commercial banks, and ensures "just-in-time" release of funds for public expenditures. As mentioned in reply to part (a) above, revolving working capital is not provided to VDVKs under PMJVM / PM-JANMAN schemes.

Operational VDVKs are encouraged to graduate into Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs) for value addition, aggregation and market linkage based on their performance. One VDPE proposal from the State of Madhya Pradesh has been approved in principle for implementation.

A total of 148 VDVKs are operational in the state of Chhattisgarh under the PM-JANMAN and PMJVM Schemes. Revolving funds amounting to ₹153.66 crores have been released to Chhattisgarh SIA for procurement of MFPs since 2013-14 through which MFPs worth ₹467 crores have been procured by the State till 2025-26. Chhattisgarh SIA has submitted the claim for reimbursement of losses under the MSP operations which is under examination. No proposal for procurement of MFPs has been received from the State of Chhattisgarh during the current financial year.

The matter has been discussed with the SIAs, and they have been advised to devise appropriate mechanisms for transferring funds directly to the bank accounts of VDVKs and ground-level primary procurement agencies. In some States, funds are already being transferred directly to the bank accounts of VDVKs.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
STATUS OF EMRSs
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the scheme of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for providing quality education to tribal students in their own environment preserving local art and culture. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country having 156593 students enrolled during the Academic Session 2025-26. In the State of Telangana 23 EMRSs have been sanctioned and all of them are functional with10199 students enrolled during the Academic Session 2025-26.

Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and sports facilities in EMRSs across the country such as well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on apparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc.

The preservation and promotion of tribal culture, language and traditional knowledge are integral to the objective of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) Scheme. To achieve this, Tribal Corners have been established in EMRSs to showcase and preserve the culture, traditions, art, crafts and heritage of tribal communities. Cultural Programs, Meets and workshops are organized to provide a platform for students to learn about, appreciate and celebrate the diverse tribal cultures and traditions of the country. Further, Regional Language Teachers are recruited in EMRSs enabling students to learn and preserve their regional languages.

The Status of schools sanctioned and operational under the EMRS scheme in the State of Telangana is given at Annexure.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Semiconductor and AI Revolution
Powering the Future
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi

Powering the Future

From Chips to AI: Building India’s Technology Leadership

Semiconductors are the foundation of modern technology, powering everything from smartphones and vehicles to satellites and AI systems. AI is now accelerating the demand for advanced chips, specialised processors and high-performance computing, making the two technologies increasingly inseparable. Recognising this convergence, India is building capabilities from chip design and fabrication to computing infrastructure and indigenous AI models. Government initiatives across both sectors are creating an integrated technology ecosystem that strengthens self-reliance, supply-chain resilience and innovation. This convergence is also opening new opportunities in advanced manufacturing, research, entrepreneurship and high-value employment. As India marks its 80th Independence Day, these capabilities mark a decisive step towards global technology leadership and a Viksit Bharat.

Semiconductors: Foundation for Technological Self-Reliance

India is building domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain, from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, equipment and materials. By strengthening domestic capabilities today, India is positioning itself to shape the technologies of tomorrow.

Dedicated Mission Laid The Foundation For Self-Reliance

  • Semicon 1.0 laid the foundation with a ₹76,000 crore outlay to build India’s semiconductor ecosystem.
  • It supports the entire value chain, spanning chip design, fabrication, packaging, testing, equipment, materials and skilled talent etc.
  • Semicon 2.0 is scaling this foundation into global ecosystem leadership, with a ₹1,27,500 crore outlay approved in July 2026.
  • Six strategic pillars drive Semicon India 2.0: chip design, semiconductor equipment and materials, fabrication facilities, advanced packaging, research and development, and talent development.

This integrated approach strengthens supply-chain resilience, expands domestic value addition and positions India for future semiconductor leadership.

From Policy to Semiconductor Manufacturing

  • 12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states, with investments commitments exceeding ₹1.64 lakh crore.
  • Projects span silicon and compound semiconductor fabs, display fabrication and advanced packaging facilities.
  • Three facilities have already commenced commercial production, marking India’s transition from semiconductor policy to manufacturing.

Semiconductor facilities will supply critical components for automobiles, telecommunications, aerospace, power electronics and consumer electronics

  • Semiconductor fabs plants that build raw silicon wafers into functioning integrated circuits and microchips.
  • Display fabrication are Plants that build flat and flexible screens for phones, cars, and gadgets etc.
  • Advanced packaging methods that encase, wire, and shield fragile chips to make them run faster and last longer.

Developing Indigenous Semiconductor Design Capabilities

  • To meet future workforce requirements, the Government has prioritised semiconductor skilling through initiatives such as Chips to Startup (C2S), under which,
  • Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools have been deployed in 320 academic institutions and
  • Over 68,000 students trained, expanding access to advanced chip-design capabilities. Click to Read More About: Chips to Start-up (C2S) Programme
  • 24 semiconductor design projects have also been approved for financial support and 105 startups/MSMEs for EDA tool support under DLI Scheme. Click to Read More About: Design Linked Incentive Scheme

Electronic Design Automation (EDA)

EDA tools are software platforms used to design, simulate, verify and optimize semiconductor chips. They manage complex chip designs, detect errors before manufacturing, and improve performance, power efficiency and reliability. By reducing design time, costs and manufacturing risks, EDA tools enable faster development of advanced chips for various applications.

 

  • 211 chips were taped out by 75 institutions by April 2026, demonstrating growing domestic design capabilities.
  • 7 chips have been successfully fabricated at various nodes including advanced nodes such as 12 nm.
  • Semicon 2.0 will further intended to support semiconductor IP, chip and system designs, strengthening India’s position as a global semiconductor design hub.

Global Partnerships

  • Global partnerships with the United States, Japan, Singapore, the Netherlands, Germany and the European Union are strengthening technology collaboration and ecosystem development.
  • Semicon India 2025 brought together 350+ exhibitors and participants from 48 countries and regions, strengthening India’s global semiconductor engagement.
  • The event recorded 35,000 registrations, 30,000 footfalls and 25,000 online viewers, reflecting strong global interest in India’s semiconductor ambitions.
  • 12 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) were announced to strengthen product development, services and semiconductor skill development.

These partnerships are helping integrate Indian companies into global semiconductor value chains and accelerate domestic capabilities.

IndiaAI Mission: Building India’s Sovereign and Inclusive AI Ecosystem

The IndiaAI Mission, approved with an outlay of about ₹10,372 crore, has made significant strides over the past year. The Mission`s ambition is focused on building capabilities that are secure, inclusive and rooted in Indian needs. It aims to make AI a strategic capability for innovation, economic growth and public service delivery.

Sovereign AI Computing Capacity At Scale

  • The IndiaAI Mission has expanded shared compute capacity to 45,000+ Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), as of June 2026.
  • By August 2026, 237 projects had accessed subsidised AI computing, covering 93.18 lakh GPU hours. This provides affordable high-performance computing for AI model development, training, testing and research, lowering entry barriers for Indian researchers, start-ups and innovators.

 

Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)

A GPU is a specialised electronic processor designed to accelerate graphics, image processing and other data-intensive computing tasks. GPUs are widely used in computers, smartphones, servers and other digital devices.

 

Foundational AI Models

  • From 506 applications received, the Government has selected 20 indigenous foundation model proposals, including 12 Large Multimodal Models and 8 Small Language Models.
  • This strengthens India’s capabilities in developing AI models suited to Indian languages, needs and contexts.

 

Digital Backbone For AI Models

  • As of July 2026, AI Kosh hosts over 14,000 datasets and 331 AI models, providing researchers, developers and innovators access to critical resources for building and scaling AI solutions.

 

From Laboratories To Real-World Governance

  • As on Aug 2026, IndiaAI initiatives have developed 62 AI prototypes and deployed 20 AI solutions across public-sector institutions.
  • 11 national-level hackathons and innovation challenges are further expanding the pipeline from ideas to deployable solutions.

 

Innovation Via Centres Of Excellences

  • As on Aug 2026, 58 Artificial Intelligence Centres of Excellence (AI CoEs) have been approved across States and Union Territories.
  • 22 CoE already approved and initiated across 13 States/UTs.
  • These centres are strengthening domain-specific research, innovation and application development.

 

Building The Talent And Deep-Tech Ecosystem

  • The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) has established 25 Technology Innovation Hubs across leading academic institutions.
  • These hubs support research, skills, start-ups and technology transfer across AI, robotics, cybersecurity, quantum technologies and other emerging fields.

 

Trusted AI Alongside Rapid Adoption

  • As of July 2026, the Indian government approved 13 Responsible AI projects under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar of the IndiaAI Mission. These projects tackle critical challenges like bias mitigation, machine unlearning, deepfake detection, privacy-preserving AI, explainability, and AI risk assessment.

 

Expansion of Data Centre Capacity to Support AI Infrastructure

  • Data centres are located across the country such as Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Gujarat.
  • The installed capacity has grown from 375 MW in 2020 to current capacity of about 1,575 MW.
  • The Data Centre industry is now further expanding in states like Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh & West Bengal which are coming up with new investment destinations.

Global Recognition

  • The Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Report 2025 ranked India third globally in AI competitiveness and ecosystem vibrancy.
  • In 2025, India was the second-largest contributor to GitHub AI projects, reflecting the strength of its developer and innovation community.
  • The India AI Impact Summit 2026 was held in February 2026. Participation from delegations from more than 100 countries and 20 international organisations, with the declaration adopted by 92 countries and organisations.
  • India joined the Pax Silica coalition at the India AI Impact Summit 2026, working with the United States and other partners to strengthen resilient global silicon supply chains.
  • This complements India’s domestic efforts to build a self-reliant, inclusive and globally competitive AI ecosystem.

Sustaining Momentum in Chips and AI

India’s semiconductor programme is progressing from approvals and design support to commercial production. The next phase, Semicon 2.0, broadens the focus to equipment, materials, advanced packaging, research, indigenous intellectual property and talent. The IndiaAI Mission is building shared compute and supporting applications across government, industry, academia and start-ups. This integrated approach is strengthening technology capabilities, enabling responsible AI governance and supporting sustained innovation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: iGOT MISSION KARMAYOGI IN WEST BENGAL
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:24PM by PIB Delhi

Presently 90,276 civil servants from West Bengal have been onboarded on the iGOT Karmayogi platform. The Government of West Bengal has not yet signed the tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) under Mission Karmayogi.

So far, eight draft Capacity Building Plans (CBPs) have been prepared for Government of West Bengal's priority departments. The iGOT Karmayogi digital learning platform hosts over 5,600 courses covering domain, functional and behavioural competencies. These courses are available for consumption for all registered users including those from West Bengal. As on date, 10,493 course completions have been recorded by learners from West Bengal. Further, all employees of the Central Government and officers of the All India Services, including those serving in West Bengal have to mandatorily complete prescribed courses annually on iGOT which gets reflected in their respective APARs for the corresponding period.

The DoPT, along with the other implementing agencies of Mission Karmayogi – Capacity Building Commission (CBC), and SPV Karmayogi Bharat (KB) are supporting the Government of West Bengal in its capacity building initiatives including handholding for the adoption of the role-based competency framework, onboarding on the iGOT platform, and integrating iGOT with other HR platforms/tools. A Programme Coordinator from CBC and an Assistant Manager from KB serve as Nodal Officers for the state of West Bengal for this purpose. DoPT also supports targeted capacity building activities in all states/UTs, including West Bengal, through the Training for All (TFA) scheme.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ZERO LITIGATION PENSION ECOSYSTEM
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare is the nodal Department for formulation of policies relating to pension and other retirement benefits of Central Government Civil employees. The 2nd National Workshop on Pension Litigation was convened in pursuance of Government's directives on effective and efficient management of litigation with focus on enhancing coordination and strengthening the capacity/skills of the Nodal officers and panel lawyers of all the Ministries/Departments handling Pension related litigation and its monitoring. It had deliberations and presentations from speakers on the best practices, systemic reforms and grievance redressals to minimize pension litigation towards welfare of pensioners and good governance. The Compendium of case laws and flyer, launched in the Workshop, outlined the best practices in handling pension litigation and recent judicial pronouncements in recurring pension litigation matters providing a comprehensive overview of the concerned pension related policies.

The compendium and flyer underscored the importance of a coordinated approach to managing pension litigation. Pension litigation is not centrally handled by any Department, it is handled on behalf of the Central Government separately by all respective Departments. For minimising litigation, Special Campaign 3 was also launched, wherein focus is on the redressal of the long pending grievances/claims and the issues. This campaign along with other initiatives viz. Pension Adalats and Inter-Ministerial Review Meetings on long pending grievances is an attempt to resolve the grievances, thereby obviating the need to approach courts of law with the resultant effect of reduction in litigation. Further, the Department, based on the clarification and advices sought by various Ministries and Departments, issues Office Memoranda to clarify the rule position to bring ease in the life of the pensioners including super-senior pensioners. The Department, has issued the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 revised it further by CCS(Pension) Rules, 2021. To ease eligibility conditions of family pensioners, Rule 50 of the said Rules (erstwhile Rule 54 of Rules of 1972) has been provided for various categories of family pensioners including divorced and disabled daughters.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Empowering Youth, Transforming India
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 1:18PM by PIB Delhi

Amrit Peedhi for Viksit Bharat@2047

India is home to one of the world’s largest youth populations, with nearly 65 percent of its citizens below the age of 35. Over the years, the Government has expanded investment across education, skilling, employment, entrepreneurship, sports, health, and civic participation to convert this demographic advantage into a development dividend. Together, these efforts are enabling the Amrit Peedhi to shape Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

MY Bharat: A Platform for Youth-Led Development

At the centre of this vision is Mera Yuva Bharat, launched in October 2023 for youth aged 15–29. The technology-enabled platform brings volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, career support and civic participation into a single nationwide ecosystem.

  • Growing national platform – More than 2.22 crore youth have registered on the platform for volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, and career opportunities, as of July 2026.
  • Volunteering at scale – Over 1.52 lakh volunteering opportunities enable young people to participate in community service, environmental action, cultural initiatives and public programmes.
  • Learning through experience – More than 24,900 experiential learning programmes have connected youth with governance, healthcare, media, technology and public service.

Digital Engagement and Civic Participation

  • Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2026 – More than 50 lakh youth participated through a nationwide quiz. The dialogue also involved 78 diaspora youth from 21 countries and identified 6,000 young leaders for a district-wise repository.
  • National Service Scheme (NSS) – Volunteer enrolment increased from 34.09 lakh in 2014–15 to 38.90 lakh in 2025–26.

Education: Access, Quality and Future-Readiness

The education ecosystem has expanded while becoming more flexible, digital and innovation-driven. National Education Policy 2020 places the learner at the centre and links schooling, higher education, skills and employability.

  • One of the world’s largest school systems – India has 14.67 lakh schools serving 24.72 crore students, supported by more than 1.02 crore teachers.
  • Improved retention – The secondary-school dropout rate declined from 14.54 % in 2013–14 to 7 in 2025–26.
  • Digital classrooms – Over 1.49 lakh schools were covered under ICT and digital initiatives by 2025–26, with more than 1.76 lakh smart classrooms and 1.79 lakh ICT laboratories sanctioned (as of March 2026).
  • Atal Tinkering Labs – More than 10,000 labs have engaged over 1.1 crore student innovators and supported more than 16 lakh projects.

Higher Education and Innovation

  • Rising enrolment – Higher-education enrolment increased from 3.4 crore in 2014–15 to 4.5 crore in 2023–24; Female enrolment increased 42.2% since 2014-2015 to 2.2 crores in 2023-24.
  • Institutional growth
     


 

  • Incubation and research – 85 Atal Incubation Centres have created 32,000+ jobs and supported over 2,900 startups.

Flexible Learning and Digital Access

  • National Credit Framework – More than 700 universities and over 7,500 affiliated colleges have adopted the National Credit Framework (NCrF).
  • Academic Bank of Credits – 3,123 institutions have been onboarded and more than 35.27 crore APAAR IDs issued, enabling learners to store, transfer, and redeem credits. (as on 12th August 2026).
  • SWAYAM – As on 12th August 2026, the platform offers more than 20,370 courses and has recorded 6.5 crore+ enrolments.
  • DIKSHA – Across India, 342 courses have recorded 19.06 crore enrolments, 15.02 crore completions, and the issuance of 13 crore certificates (as on 12th August 2026).

Skilling and Employability

The Government has empowered over 6 crore people through its skilling initiatives. Skill India Mission has shifted training from basic certification towards a demand-led model connected with industry, apprenticeships, digital platforms, and emerging technologies.

  • Lower unemployment – The unemployment rate declined from 7.71 per cent in 2014 to 4.2 per cent in 2025.
  • Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) – More than 1.64 crore youth have been trained across four phases since 2015. PMKVY includes industry-linked training in AI, robotics, drones, electronics, green energy, and other future-facing sectors, with on-the-job exposure.
  • Jan Shikshan Sansthan – 36.48 lakh people were trained till March 2026.
  • National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) – More than 54.41 lakh apprentices were engaged till March 2026.
  • Startup India – The number of startups grew from about 350 before 2014 to more than 2.47 lakh by August 2026, making India the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem.
  • Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme - As of 12th August, 2026, the PM Internship Scheme has provided 1,64,902 internship opportunities across 31 sectors.
  • PM-SETU – Launched in October 2025 with an estimated outlay of ₹60,000 crore to upgrade 1,000 government ITIs through 200 hubs and 800 spokes, with industry participation and labor-market-led courses.
  • Between 2014 and 2025, ITIs increased from 9,977 to 14,688; enrolment from 9.5 lakh to 14.7 lakh; National Skill Training Institutes from 25 to 33; and Institutes for Training of
  • Trainers from 11 to 120.

Sports and Fitness

India has built a structured sports pathway that begins with local talent identification and extends to high-performance support. Sport is increasingly seen as a viable career, backed by coaching, infrastructure, scientific training and competition exposure.

  • Khelo India infrastructure – Under the scheme, 349 infrastructure projects worth ₹3,176 crore have been approved, alongside the establishment of 1,067 Khelo India Centres and 267 academies. The scheme also supports 2,745 athletes.
  • Khelo India Games – Since 2018, more than 63,000 athletes have participated in the Youth, University, Winter, Para, Beach, Water Sports and Tribal Games.
  • Support for elite athletes – The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) supports 51 Core, 52 Para Core and 130 Development athletes. Core and Development athletes receive monthly stipends of ₹50,000 and ₹25,000, respectively.
  • Expanded investment – The revamped Khelo India Scheme and enhanced support for National Sports Federations have a combined outlay of ₹36,441 crore for the period 2026–27 to 2030–31.

Health and Well-being

Youth empowerment depends on physical, mental, and preventive healthcare. Government programmes have expanded adolescent-friendly services, mental-health counselling, substance-abuse awareness, and access to comprehensive primary care.

  • Adolescent health – Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHCs) increased from 6,619 in 2014–15 to 7,203 in 2021–22. Adolescents receiving clinical and counselling services rose from 39 lakh to 82 lakh in the same period; 97.67 lakh youth registered in the clinic in 2024–25 up to November 2024.
  • Mental health – Tele-MANAS has handled over 43.70 lakh calls through 53 cells, supported by 23 mentoring institutes and five Regional Coordinating Centres (as on 12th August 2026).
  • Substance-abuse prevention – As on 12th August, 2026, Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has reached over 30.05 crore people, including 11.86 crore youth. More than 28.56 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while over 28.29 lakh persons have received treatment and rehabilitation support.

A Decade of Transformation

Twelve years of sustained, multi-sectoral investment have produced a measurable transformation in India’s youth. More young Indians are staying in education, acquiring industry-relevant skills, entering formal employment, creating businesses, participating in community life, and competing at the highest levels of sport.

The shift has been from access to opportunity, from participation to leadership, and from youth as beneficiaries to youth as co-creators. Policy, institutions, and digital platforms have laid a strong foundation; the Amrit Peedhi is carrying it forward towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Expanding the Development Horizon
Ensuring Welfare, Inclusion, and Empowerment for Rural and Tribal Communities
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 12:27PM by PIB Delhi

India’s development story is reaching deeper into rural and tribal communities, transforming access, opportunity, and quality of life. From basic services and resilient infrastructure to livelihoods, skills, education, and financial security, interventions are expanding the foundations of inclusive growth. Focused efforts for women, tribal communities, and vulnerable groups are further strengthening pathways to dignity and empowerment. These initiatives are reshaping rural India through wider opportunity, stronger communities, and more equitable development.

From Welfare Delivery to Decentralised Partnerships

  • Direct fiscal transfers to gram panchayats have been increased. It has been increased from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15th Finance Commission (2021–26) to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16th Finance Commission (2026–31).
  • The Union Budget for rural development has been increased from ₹87,765 crore (2016–17) to ₹2.73 lakh crore (2026–27).
  • The Union Budget for tribal affairs has been increased from ₹4,826 crore (2016–17) to ₹15,421.97 crore (2026–27).

Foundations of Dignity: Universal Access to Basic Needs

Jal Jeevan Mission

  • Household tap water coverage increased from 3.23 crore (August 2019) to over 15.91 crore (August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, 2.89 lakh villages have reported 100% tap water coverage under Har Ghar Jal campaign.

Swachh Bharat Abhiyan - Grameen

  • Over 12.19 crore individual household toilets have been constructed, as of August 12, 2026.
  • India was declared Open Defecation Free in 2019.
  • Over 1,288 GOBARdhan biogas plants are operational, as of August 11, 2026, compared to 14 plants in FY 2018-19.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana

  • As of August 12, 2026, over 10.57 crore free LPG connections have been provided to women from below-poverty-line households.
  • The total number of LPG connections in India has increased from 14.52 crore in 2014 to 33.39 crore in 2026.

Universal Village Electrification

  • 100% willing household electrification (pan-India level) was achieved by March 2019 under PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA).
  • Under the Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana, 100% village electrification was achieved by 2025.

Ayushman Bharat

  • More than 45.51 crore Ayushman Cards have been issued as of August 12, 2026.
  • 96.43 crore ABHA accounts have been created as of August 12, 2026.
  • Over 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are currently functional (as of August 12, 2026).

Food Security for All

  • PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides free foodgrains to over 81.35 crore beneficiaries.
  • 99.8% Fair Price Shops under the PDS are automated for Aadhaar-based distribution, as of July 29, 2026.
  • Ration cards are 100% digitised across all States/UTs as of July 29, 2026.
  • As of July 29, 2026, over 221 crore portability transactions have been recorded under One Nation One Ration Card.

Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan)

  • Between 2018-19 to 2025-26, 4,073 schools have been upgraded and 1.49 lakh ICT and digital initiatives implemented. Further, 25,000 schools are covered under skill education.
  • 97.3% of the schools are equipped with functional female sanitation facilities.
  • Female drop-out rate at primary school level decreased from 4.6% (2013-14) to 0.1% (2025-26). At secondary school level, it reduced from 14.5% (2013-14) to 8% (2025-26).

Reservation for Economically Weaker Section and Improved Enrolment Levels

  • 10% EWS reservation provided for candidates outside existing SC, ST, and OBC reservation categories in 2019. This decision benefits the economically disadvantaged individuals from the general category.
  • In 2025-26, Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) was recorded 89.4 at primary level and 81.5 at secondary level. GER at higher secondary level increased to 61.7 in 2025-26 as compared to 46.4 in 2014-15.

Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

  • Girls’ Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) for girls at the secondary level (Classes 9–10) rose from 75.5% in 2014–15 to 83.4% in 2025–26.

Kasturba Balika Vidyalayas and PM eVidya

  • The number of sanctioned schools increased from 3,609 (2014–15) to 5,639 (2024-25). Operational KGBVs stand at 5,133, as of 2024–25.
  • Enrolment increased from 3.52 lakh (2014–15) to 7.11 lakh (2024).
  • The SWAYAM portal (India’s indigenous MOOC platform) has over 6.5 crore enrolments (as of August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, DIKSHA has 2.35 crore registered users.

Building the Backbone: Infrastructure and Connectivity

 

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Grameen

  • Under PMAY-G, over 3.91 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 3.13 crore houses have been completed (as of August 12, 2026).

Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana

  • As of June 2026, 99.6% of eligible habitations have been connected with all-weather roads.
  • Completed length of roads increased from 3.86 lakh km (May 2000 – May 2014) to 4.13 lakh km (May 2014 – August 12, 2026).
  • Completed number of bridges rose from 484 to 10,404 during May 2014 – August 12, 2026.

Digitalization of Gram Panchayats

  • Under BharatNet, 2.19 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) are connected as of May 2026.
  • Through eGramSwaraj, over ₹3 lakh crore in payments have been processed, as of June 2026.
  • Over 1.28 lakh GPs are using SabhaSaar for creating meeting summaries, as of June 2026.

Pathways to Prosperity: Livelihoods, Skills, and Financial Security

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)

  • As of August 12, 2026, 10.19 crore households have been mobilised into 94.46 lakh SHGs.
  • As of July 29, 2026, 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis have been created.

Role of Community Resource Persons in Ensuring Last-Mile Delivery of Schemes

  • Over 9 lakh CRPs are currently active, serving thematic areas like agriculture, banking, insurance and nutrition.
  • This includes more than 50,548 Bank Sakhis, 1.91 lakh Krishi Sakhis, 2,012 Matsya Sakhis, and 1.70 lakh Pashu Sakhis.

Introduction of Self-Help Entrepreneur Mart (SHE-Mart)

  • Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, aiming to benefit 1 crore women.
  • Aims to create community-owned retail spaces for women under the SHG ecosystem.

Deendayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana

  • Candidates trained increased from 43,038 in 2014–15 to 18.45 lakh till August 11, 2026.
  • Candidates placed rose from 21,446 in 2014–15 to 12.35 lakh till August 11, 2026.

Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana

  • Over 1.64 crore youth have received skill training since inception till June 2026.

Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)

  • Total persondays generated between FY 2006-07 to FY 2013-14 were 1,660 crore, whereas, between FY 2014-15 to FY 2024-25, it rose to 3,029 crore.
  • Women’s participation increased from 48% (FY 2013–14) to 58.19% (FY 2024–25).

e-Shram Portal

  • Registrations increased from 14.40 crore (Dec 2021) to 31.87 crore (August 12, 2026).

PM Vishwakarma Yojana

  • As of August 12, 2026, over 30 lakh traditional artisans have been registered.
  • As of August 12, 2026, 24.32 lakh artisans have received skill training and 17.70 lakh have received toolkits.

PM SVANidhi

  • Number of beneficiaries has increased from 26.37 lakh (Nov 2021) to 78.17 lakh (August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, loans amounting to ₹18,971.18 crore have been disbursed. 46% of the beneficiaries are women.

PM MUDRA Yojana

  • Total number of loans sanctioned have increased from 3.49 crore (2016) to over 59.14 crore (July 2026).

PM Jan Dhan Yojana

  • Number of beneficiaries have increased from 17.9 crore (Aug 2015) to 58.90 crore (August 12, 2026).

Expanding Social Security Coverage

  • Under National Pension System, beneficiaries increased from 1.05 crore (2016–17) to 2.17 crore (2025–26).
  • Under Atal Pension Yojana, beneficiaries increased from 48.80 lakh (2016–17) to 9.29 crore (June 2026).
  • 27.90 crore people covered by Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana up to July 2026.
  • 58.78 crore people covered under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana up to July 1, 2026.
  • More than 54 lakh unorganised sector workers have been registered under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan scheme as of July 2026.

Accelerating Tribal Development through Integrated Interventions

Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN)

  • As of August 5, 2026, 540 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) have been sanctioned, benefiting 46,042 persons from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.

 

Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PM-JVM)

  • 4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras sanctioned, benefitting 12.48 lakh tribals under this scheme, as of August 2026.

Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA)

It combines the efforts of 17 ministries and focuses on filling long-standing gaps in tribal-majority villages and PVTG habitations. Under PM JUGA, the emphasis has increasingly moved from isolated interventions to coordinated, mission-mode delivery across sectors and ministries. In last 12 years-

  • 7.60 lakh tribal houses have been completed and 28,303 tribal villages have access to drinking water.
  • 59,812 tribal households and public institutions have been electrified and 657 Anganwadi Centres have been operationalized in tribal areas.
  • 692 hostels have also sanctioned for tribal students.

Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)

  • As of August 12, 2026, over 4.16 lakh Scheduled Caste (SC) houses have been built, over 4.17 lakh SC households are covered under health protection schemes, and more than 3.57 lakh SC households have individual toilets.
  • 17,578 villages have been declared Adarsh Grams as of August 12, 2026.

Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs)

  • Operational schools increased from 129 (2014–15) to 511 (August 12, 2026).
  • As of August 12, 2026, EMRSs have an enrolment of 1.68 lakh students.

PM-YASASVI

  • 20.61 lakh students have received pre-matric scholarship, and 24.53 lakh students have received post-matric scholarship for FY 2024-25.

Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe (ST) Students

  • Between April 2024 and August 12, 2026, Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme has benefitted more than 28.99 lakh tribal students.
  • National Fellowship for ST Students supported 2,961 research scholars in 2025–26. 56% of the beneficiaries were females.

Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)

  • The Top-Class Education for SC Students scheme enabled 8,571 students to study in leading institutions such as IITs, IIMs, NITs and AIIMS in 2025-26.

National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE)

  • 89,915 sewer and septic tank workers and more than 2.81 lakh waste pickers have been validated as of July 2026.

Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-Notified Tribes (SEED)

  • During 2025-26, ₹26.75 crore was disbursed for the educational empowerment of 4,485 De-Notified Tribe (DNT) students.
  • 73,569 Ayushman Bharat cards have been issued to DNT families, under the health component, during 2025-26.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Biodiversity Authority releases Rs. 15.52 crore ABS Proceeds from Mustard Genetic Resources
Amount to be shared among 26 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils based on Mustard cultivation area
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:44AM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has released Rs. 15.52 crore in Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) proceeds from M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation, which developed ten commercial mustard (Brassica juncea) hybrid varieties using India's biological resources. The amount will flow to 26 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), with the ABS share calculated based on the area under mustard cultivation in each State.

M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation bred the ten varieties in-house but the parental lines were sourced from the open market and traders. As no single farmer or community could be identified as the source, the NBA constituted an Expert Committee to work out the modalities for ABS disbursal in such cases.

The modalities suggested by the Expert Committee were approved by the Authority. Accordingly, in cases where biological resources are accessed from intermediaries, the ABS is to be shared among the SBBs/UTBCs where the resource is cultivated. The NBA sourced cultivation-area figures from the ICAR–Indian Institute of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (ICAR-IIRMR), Bharatpur, Rajasthan, and used them to calculate each State's share.

Rajasthan, which accounts for nearly 42 per cent of India's mustard cultivation, is receiving the highest benefit, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. As mustard cultivation is spread across the country, almost every State and Union Territory receives a share proportionately. The top ten ABS receiving States are:

0.67

Every SBB and UTBC has to utilise the ABS amount as per Section 32 of the Biological Diversity Act, which includes conservation-linked work; documenting and updating People's Biodiversity Registers; in-situ and ex-situ conservation of biodiversity; restoring degraded ecosystems; strengthening Biodiversity Heritage Sites; building the capacity of Biodiversity Management Committees; improving community livelihoods, among other activities.

The release is part of the NBA's ongoing effort under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, to ensure that when India's genetic resources create commercial value, a fair share flows back to conservation and to the States and communities that sustain that diversity, in line with the Nagoya Protocol and Target 13 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on fair and equitable benefit sharing.

The NBA has released a total ABS amount of Rs. 182.5 crore so far. It has released Rs. 116.22 crore to beneficiaries across the country in the last 12 months.

About the National Biodiversity Authority

The National Biodiversity Authority is a statutory body established under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, functioning under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. It regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol's principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits.
